title.narrative: Emergency cholera response in Unity State

description.narrative: Cordaid would like to consider provision of effective cholera treatment and prevention services to vulnerable populations through set up oral rehydration points (ORPs), cholera treatment facilities (CTUs/CTCs), and health care workers training on treatment protocols. Adequate supplies are available and job aids are in place. Cordaid will ensure that ORPs and CTUs/CTCs are accessible to the most-affected populations, work closely with epidemiology and logistics to predict supply needs and pre-position them as needed. And to ensure effective case management Cordaid will train health-care workers on the use of RDTs, specimen collection and transport procedures. The project team will work closely with WaSH and logistics colleagues to ensure adequate IPC in treatment structures.

South Sudan is one of the cholera endemic countries in the Africa region, the country has so far experienced ten (10) major cholera outbreaks (1980 – 2017) of varying magnitude from 17 to 48,035 cases, with case fatality rates (CFR) ranging between 0.13% and 2.9%. All outbreaks started in Juba except the recent 2022 outbreak with its epi center in Bentiu, Rubkona Unity State. The key drivers to cholera outbreaks include poor WASH conditions, complex humanitarian conditions and changing climatic patterns worsening socio-economic conditions. South Sudanese continue to face challenges of access to safe and clean water and 59% of the population have no access to safe and clean drinking water. In addition, 60% of the population practice open defecation. On 8th October the government of Republic of South Sudan received report of suspected cholera case and on 28th October the government of South Sudan declared cholera outbreak in Renk County of Upper Nile State. Since then, the cholera outbreak spread to Juba, Malakal, Aweil West, Aweil East, Aweil Center, Canal/Pigi, Rubkona, Guit, Mayom and Pariang Counties. As of 30th December 2024 a cumulative total number of 9,707have been reported with 180 death CRF of 1.9%. Cordaid is running two Cholera treatment Units in Bentiu State Hospital and Rubkona PHCC in Rubkona County.
Total beneficiaries: 253,174 Women: 48,382 Children: 103,801 Men: 50,357 Elderly: 10,127
